definitions.gloss: to compromise; to make concessions; to settle; to meet halfway
definitions.explanation: To reach an agreement by both sides making concessions. Can also mean to lower one's standards or accept something less than ideal.

examples.japanese: お{互|たが}いに{妥協|だきょう}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to compromise with each other.

examples.japanese: {品質|ひんしつ}に{関|かん}しては{一切|いっさい}{妥協|だきょう}しない。
examples.english: We make absolutely no compromises when it comes to quality.

examples.japanese: {予算|よさん}の{都合|つごう}で{妥協|だきょう}せざるを{得|え}なかった。
examples.english: We had no choice but to compromise due to budget constraints.

notes:
USAGE:
Can have either a neutral sense (healthy compromise in negotiations) or a negative sense (settling for less, lowering standards). The phrase {妥協|だきょう}しない (to not compromise) is often used positively to express high standards or dedication.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {妥協|だきょう}する (to compromise)
- {妥協|だきょう}しない (to not compromise)
- {妥協|だきょう}{点|てん} (point of compromise)
- {妥協|だきょう}を{許|ゆる}さない (to allow no compromise)
- {妥協|だきょう}{案|あん} (compromise proposal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {譲歩|じょうほ}する: to make concessions — focuses on one side yielding
- {折|お}り{合|あ}う: to come to terms — more informal, everyday
